query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure in high-entropy alloys can increase the coercive field by creating complex magnetization processes involving the successive reversal of magnetic vortices within A2 precipitates and interactions with a weakly ferromagnetic B2 matrix.
generation.intervention: Introducing a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure
generation.conditions: Annealing at 600°C for 15 h in an Ar atmosphere and quenching in water
generation.mechanism: Complex magnetization process involving successive reversal of magnetic vortices within A2 precipitates and interactions with a weakly ferromagnetic B2 matrix
generation.baseline: AlCoFeNi high-entropy alloy without hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure
generation.boundary: Limitations of the study include unclear interactions between different magnetic elements and the need for further work to determine the effect of external magnetic field and/or stress annealing on precipitate formation
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains regarding the specific influence mechanism of the magnetic field on the atomic-level structure and the effects of temperature, strain, or magnetic field on precipitate formation

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the coercive field of AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi high-entropy alloys with and without hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi is not significantly higher than that of AlCoFeNi, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: What is the influence of a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure on the formation of magnetic vortex states and the origin of coercivity in AlCo(Cr)FeNi high-entropy alloys?. System: AlCoFeNi and AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi high-entropy alloys. Processing: Arc melting of Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni pellets in an Ar atmosphere, followed by annealing at 600°C for 15 h in an Ar atmosphere and quenching in water. Test conditions: Bulk magnetization measured at 300 K up to 1 T; Lorentz TEM and off-axis electron holography performed in magnetic-field-free conditions and with applied out-of-plane fields up to 1.5 T; APT conducted at 60 K. Findings: AlCoFeNi has a saturation magnetization (MS) of 99.8 Am2/kg and coercivity (Hc) of 1.45 mT, while AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi has MS of 46.2 Am2/kg and Hc of 9.56 mT.; AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi exhibits a hierarchical structure with coarse A2 gen-1 (1–5 μm), medium A2 gen-2 (50-150 nm), and fine A2 gen-3 (<10 nm) phases in a B2 matrix.; A2 gen-2 precipitates in region R1 contain 3D magnetic vortex states with a magnetic induction peak of 0.5 ± 0.1 T.; The ratio of clockwise to counterclockwise magnetic vortices in A2 gen-2 precipitates is approximately
